Title: Trump says Google rejected his idea to rename ocean after him
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Friday told supporters about his alleged attempt to have an ocean named after him and Google's refusal to go along with the idea, reported German news agency dpa.
Speaking at a campaign rally in Georgia, Trump claimed he had suggested to representatives of the internet giant that either the Atlantic or Pacific Ocean be renamed the "Trump Ocean". According to Trump, they responded indignantly: "We've had it. That's enough. We're not doing any more."
Trump had already renamed the Gulf of Mexico the "Gulf of America" by executive order in 2025, followed by Lake Ontario on the Canadian border, which he renamed "Lake America" in August this year. Google Maps adopted both changes for users in the United States.
Trump told supporters he had sent Google a map labelled "Trump Ocean", but company representatives rejected the idea.
"Sir, look, okay, this one we can't do. Oceans are different. Oceans cover many, many countries. We can't do it," Trump quoted them as saying.
Trump said he had only been joking — this time — but added that it was not the worst idea he had ever had.
It was not immediately clear whether the exchange with Google had actually taken place.
Trump has repeatedly suggested that he would like to rename an ocean. He has also floated the idea of renaming the Strait of Hormuz the "Trump Strait", apparently in an attempt to provoke Iran, with which the US is at war.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia eyes bigger role in global maritime dispute resolution - Chief Justice
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's strategic location between the Straits of Melaka, one of the world's busiest shipping lanes, and the South China Sea strengthens its role in resolving international commercial and maritime disputes, said Chief Justice Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh.
He said Malaysia has long had a specialised Admiralty Court, and the establishment of the International Commercial and Admiralty Division (ICAD) has brought admiralty and international commercial cases under a single specialised division.
Established at the High Court here on March 2 this year, ICAD is expected to boost investor confidence in Kuala Lumpur as a regional hub for business and dispute resolution.
Wan Ahmad Farid said that delays of even a few days in urgent admiralty cases could have significant commercial consequences, particularly when disputes involved vessels, cargo and parties across several jurisdictions.
"Applications for the arrest or release of vessels, the provision of security and other urgent matters require prompt attention, and a delay of even a few days can have significant commercial consequences," he said in his keynote address at the inaugural ICAD Conference 2026 at the Asian International Arbitration Centre (AIAC) today.
Wan Ahmad Farid said maritime disputes were inherently international, often involving vessels registered in one country, owned by companies in another, financed by banks in a third and carrying cargo belonging to parties across several jurisdictions.
"A vessel may be registered in one country, owned by a company in another, financed by a bank in a third, chartered by an entity in a fourth, and carrying cargo belonging to parties in several more.
"Admiralty disputes are inherently international, involving vessel arrests, charterparty disputes, cargo claims, maritime security and arbitration.
"The trade that passes through generates disputes over cargo, charterparties, finance, insurance, energy and infrastructure,'  he said.
He said geography alone is not enough as ICAD's role is to transform Malaysia's geographical advantage into a jurisdictional advantage by ensuring disputes could be resolved close to where the business is done, by judges who understand its commercial and maritime context.
He said a premier dispute resolution forum was built on trust, which could not be bought or established overnight but had to be earned over time.
"It is earned when foreign investors know that if they bring a dispute to Malaysia, they will receive justice that is blind to nationality, deeply sophisticated in commercial logic and fiercely independent.
"Roads and ports carry goods. Certainty and trust carry confidence, and confidence carries capital.
"Let us build this infrastructure deliberately, protect it carefully, and offer it to the world with integrity," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Local cocoa production needs boost to cut import reliance
Article:
MELAKA: Malaysia needs to boost local cocoa bean production to reduce reliance on imports, as the processing industry depends heavily on foreign supplies.
Plantation and Commodities Minister Datuk Seri Dr Noraini Ahmad said stronger local production was needed to strengthen the cocoa supply chain and ensure growers benefited from the industry's expansion.
She said Malaysia's exports of cocoa beans and cocoa-based products rose from RM15.06 billion in 2024 to RM18.33 billion last year, highlighting the industry's growth potential.
However, growth in cocoa processing needed to be matched by higher local bean production so growers could also benefit, she said when opening A Malaysian Cocoa Affair 2026, organised by the Malaysian Cocoa Board (MCB) at a shopping centre in Banda Hilir today.
Also present were Plantation and Commodities Ministry secretary-general Datuk Yusran Shah Mohd Yusof and MCB director-general Shari Fuddin Sha'ari.
The ministry is focusing on increasing local production and smallholders' incomes through group planting, rehabilitating less productive farms and providing planting materials from high-quality cocoa clones.
"We do not want the industry to grow only at the processing level while local growers fail to receive their fair share of the benefits," Noraini said.
The ministry is also strengthening the National Cocoa Traceability System to identify the origin of cocoa beans and record their movement from farms to processing facilities.
Noraini said this was important to ensure
Malaysian cocoa products
met international market requirements, including the European Union Deforestation Regulation.
More than RM40 million was allocated under 2027 Budget to support the development of high-value cocoa products using modern technology, including premium chocolate made through the bean-to-bar method, she said.
Malaysia also aims to develop more local chocolate brands capable of entering international markets.
Noraini encouraged more young people to enter the cocoa industry, including in chocolate making, product design, marketing, research and entrepreneurship, to strengthen the sector's future.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Customs officer died from pressure to neck, post-mortem finds
Article:
SEREMBAN: A post-mortem found that a female civil servant who was found murdered in Nilai on Thursday died from pressure applied to her neck.
Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the cause of death was determined following a five-hour post-mortem at the Forensic Medicine Department of Hospital Tuanku Ja'afar (HTJ) here today.
"The post-mortem was conducted from 9.40am to 2.30pm by Dr Akma Nurain Fairuz Mahamad Arif at HTJ today.
"Initial findings indicate that the cause of death was pressure applied to the neck region," he said in a statement.
However, Alzafny noted that physical examinations also uncovered three stab wounds caused by a sharp weapon — two to the abdomen and one to the right cheek.
The remains of Norhazwani Ibrahim, 35, were brought out of the HTJ Forensic Medicine Department at 3pm immediately after documentation was completed.
Her remains were transported to the KLIA Quarters Mosque in Nilai in a Customs Department hearse for funeral prayers before being brought back to Kelantan for burial.
Several family members, colleagues, and representatives from the Customs Department and the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) were present at the hospital throughout the post-mortem.
It was previously reported that the victim's husband surrendered at the Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi police station in Sepang, Selangor, admitting to killing his wife at a government quarters in Nilai.
Alzafny said the
suspect has been remanded for seven days
starting Friday to assist investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
In Machang, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the suspect, 35, had a history of imprisonment for drug-related offences and had recently been released from prison.
"The suspect was just released from prison and has a history of imprisonment related to drug offences. That is what we can confirm," he told reporters after the Home Ministry's Kampung Angkat Madani and Sekolah Angkat Madani programmes at Sekolah Kebangsaan Jambu Lawar today.
Saifuddin said Norhazwani's remains would be transported by road to Tumpat, Kelantan, and were expected to arrive tonight.
He added that the victim leaves behind two children, aged five and six, and expressed hope that he would be able to attend the funeral, subject to his schedule.
It was previously reported that Norhazwani, a Customs officer, was found murdered at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) quarters on Thursday, with her husband named as the suspect.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 10 complaints lodged over suspected water-mixed RON95 petrol in Selangor
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The Selangor branch of the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry is investigating 10 complaints over viral reports of RON95 petrol allegedly mixed with water, which reportedly damaged vehicles in several areas in the state.
Its director, Muhamad Hanif Asa'ari, said field investigations and enforcement operations at seven petrol stations yesterday were conducted in response to public complaints and reports on social media.
"Field results show that 27 cans of RON95 petrol samples have been taken and seized from the affected petrol stations to be sent to the Chemistry Department for laboratory analysis," he said in a statement today.
He said initial inspections found that all the premises concerned had valid licences for controlled scheduled goods and licences under the Petroleum Development Act 1974.
However, he said notices under Section 32 of the Trade Descriptions Act 2011 had been issued, requiring petrol station operators to submit information and business-related documents to assist the investigation.
"An investigation is being conducted into the possibility of violations of Section 5(1)(c), read together with Section 6(1)(d) and Section 7 of the Trade Descriptions Act 2011, relating to allegations of false trade descriptions concerning the petrol supplied," he said.
He reminded companies and petrol station operators to ensure that underground storage tanks were regularly maintained and complied with established safety and quality standards.
"Strict action in accordance with legal provisions will be taken against any party found to have committed violations that jeopardise consumers' interests and safety," he said.
Meanwhile, he advised affected motorists to keep their official petrol receipts and workshop inspection reports as supporting documents for complaints and to assist investigations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pairin Kitingan writes life story to keep Sabah's history alive
Article:
PENAMPANG: Tan Sri Joseph Pairin Kitingan wrote a 270-page autobiography to help his grandchildren understand his life and preserve key historical events in Sabah's history.
The former Sabah chief minister said the idea came after realising that his grandchildren, particularly those studying in Australia, knew little about his life and contributions.
"I thought, as long as I have grandchildren, I have to write this book so that they will know who their grandfather is and what he has been doing," he said at the book launch at KDCA Hall.
The 86-year-old Parti Bersatu Sabah (PBS) founder said he had kept notes for years before beginning work on the autobiography seriously about five years ago.
Titled Joseph Pairin Kitingan, the book documents significant events in Sabah's history, including the 1982 Kaamatan harvest festival in Tambunan, when Pairin was told by the Berjaya government to resign from the state cabinet.
Pairin, whose pen name is "Tonnipot", meaning firefly in the Kadazan language, said he hoped the book would help readers understand not only what happened in the past, but also why events unfolded as they did and what they meant for Sabah's future.
He founded PBS on March 5, 1985, and led it to victory in the state election weeks later. He became Sabah's seventh chief minister on April 22 that year and served until March 1994.
Although PBS won 25 of 48 seats in the 1994 state election, defections by assemblymen cost the party its governing majority, prompting Pairin to resign as chief minister.
Pairin is also known as Huguan Siou, the paramount leader of the Kadazandusun community, and has championed indigenous identity and cultural preservation.
He said documenting history was important for younger generations to understand the past and help shape the state's future.
Half of the proceeds from the RM100 book will go to the Huguan Foundation for Charity and Education, which supports charitable and educational causes. Pairin said public support for the autobiography could help the foundation expand its assistance to those in need.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump blocking Russia sanctions a 'historic moment', says Putin envoy
Article:
MOSCOW: US President Donald Trump's decision to waive a new package of sanctions on Russia is a "historic moment", a Russian presidential envoy said on Saturday.
Trump signed an executive order on Friday waiving sweeping US sanctions and tariffs targeting Russia's energy revenues, two days before they were due to take effect.
The move came amid a clash with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy that has fuelled speculation that the US leader is increasingly siding with Moscow nearly five years into Russia's offensive against Ukraine, which has killed hundreds of thousands of people and displaced millions.
"The Trump administration's suspension of the Graham Act is an important and truly historic moment," Kirill Dmitriev, envoy for Russian President Vladimir Putin, said on social media.
The Kremlin and Putin — who appeared in military uniform on Friday and said Moscow intends to seize the rest of Ukraine — have yet to react to the move, which is a major diplomatic win for Russia.
The Lindsey Graham Act — named after the US senator who sponsored the bill — targeted Russia's energy and defence sectors, as well as Putin and other senior officials.
Dmitriev said the act would have caused "serious damage first and foremost to the US economy and global markets".
The West imposed sweeping sanctions on Russia when it launched its war against Ukraine in 2022.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tanker hit off Saudi Arabia's Gulf coast, crew evacuated
Article:
DUBAI: A tanker was struck by an "unknown projectile" off Saudi Arabia's Gulf coast, forcing the evacuation of its crew, a maritime monitoring agency said on Saturday.
The vessel was hit on Friday, 68 nautical miles off Jubail, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said, adding that "all crew are reported safe".
Ships have regularly come under Iranian fire during the Middle East war, as Iran blockades the Strait of Hormuz — the only exit route for oil and gas exports via the Gulf.
Vanguard, another maritime security agency, identified the ship as the Marshall Islands-flagged Safeen Principal crude oil tanker, saying it had lost power and suffered an engine-room fire.
About one-fifth of global oil exports passed through the Strait of Hormuz before the war began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran on Feb 28. Oil prices have soared during the war.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ramanan says Sungai Buloh seat secure amid strong grassroots support
Article:
SUNGAI BULOH: Sungai Buloh member of parliament Datuk Seri Ramanan Ramakrishnan considers his position in the constituency "safe", driven by strong support from residents.
Ramanan, who is also the human resources minister, said he has done his best in fulfilling his responsibilities as an MP and will continue striving to enhance his performance to meet the community's expectations.
"For me, I have done the best I can. I am still doing the best I can, and I will continue to do even better if possible," he told reporters after officiating the Sungai Buloh Madani Kita programme at Kota Damansara today.
The PKR vice-president said his secure standing is reflected in the enthusiastic turnouts at various community programmes organised in the area.
He noted that today's event drew over 1,000 visitors, offering a positive indicator of how residents view ongoing grassroots initiatives.
"Looking at what happened today, I feel this is a very comfortable journey based on the support received from the residents here," he said.
Ramanan said the event was held as an open session without participant filtering or preset questions, allowing residents to freely air grievances and raise longstanding issues.
"Various local matters were brought up, including a drainage problem that has reportedly gone unresolved since 2015. We will find the best approach to resolve these issues promptly," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Armed forces to review reserve personnel allowances
Article:
PORT DICKSON: The armed forces is reviewing allowances for its volunteer reserve personnel to encourage greater participation in training and strengthen the reserve force.
Chief of Defence Force General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman said the review was aimed at boosting commitment among reserve force members and strengthening the manpower pool for the regular armed forces.
He said the current hourly rates of RM9.80 and RM8 were relatively low, having last been reviewed around 2022.
"We want them to participate actively in training and activities organised by their respective regiments. Active involvement also gives them additional points if they wish to join the regular force, making the screening process easier," he told reporters after the passing-out parade for 1,485 recruits from the 206/26 Series of Male Young Soldiers Training today.
Malek Razak said an estimated 40 to 50 per cent of registered reserve personnel were inactive, including failing to attend training when called up.
Under existing policy, those who remain inactive for several months or years are removed from the membership list, he said, adding that this hindered efforts to maintain the territorial army as a reserve force.
"Our target is a one-to-one ratio between reserve personnel and regular armed forces personnel," he said.
To improve participation, the armed forces will diversify training methods, upgrade infrastructure and strengthen promotional efforts.
Malek Razak said graduates of the Reserve Officers Training Unit (Palapes) were given priority to join the regular armed forces through the graduate officer recruitment scheme and could also receive additional academic credits.
"We believe it is a waste for them to undergo military training, particularly as officers, only to leave after completing their studies. We want them to become the next generation of officers in the regular service," he said.
In a separate development, he said the Malaysian Battalion (MALBATT) would hand over some support assets to the Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF) following the planned termination of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (Unifil) mission early next year.
The assets include generators, general-purpose vehicles and other equipment that would not need to be returned to Malaysia.
Army chief General Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman was also present.
Earlier, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said 292 assets worth an estimated US$10 million (about RM42 million) would be handed over in stages until January 2027 for welfare, humanitarian assistance and peacekeeping efforts for local communities.
Malek Razak also urged young people to join the military, particularly in technology, artificial intelligence (AI) and information technology (IT), to support the modernisation of the armed forces.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: TVET students to get training with job guarantees
Article:
SUNGAI BULOH: The government will introduce an industrial training programme with job guarantees to improve the employability of Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) students.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the ministry had visited Bangkok, Thailand, and Singapore to establish cooperation on the programme.
He said an understanding had been reached to introduce the programme, which would include student exchanges.
The Advanced Technology Training Centres (ADTEC) would send Malaysian students to partner institutions and receive students from them, including Singapore's Institute of Technical Education (ITE).
Under
the programm
e, companies requiring specific skills from graduates would offer them temporary jobs while they received training at ADTEC.
After completing the training, they would be offered permanent positions with salaries based on the skills they had acquired.
Ramanan was speaking to the media after officiating at the Madani Kita 2026 Sungai Buloh: "Giving Meaning to the People's Hopes" programme in Kota Damansara today.
He rejected the perception that TVET graduates struggled to find jobs, saying the latest data showed their employability rate had reached 98 per cent, up from about 95.5 per cent last year.
He said the figures demonstrated the effectiveness of strategic cooperation with industry in ensuring training remained relevant and met labour market needs.
In August, the ministry announced plans for student exchanges between the Manpower Department's Advanced Technology Training Centres and ITE Singapore. The cooperation also covers knowledge sharing and the exchange of best practices in TVET.
Ramanan also said the proposed RM2,500 monthly starting basic salary for graduates and semi-skilled workers would be detailed in guidelines that would apply regardless of region or locality.
He said workers should be assessed fairly based on their qualifications, skills and abilities rather than the state or location where they worked.
Differences in location should not be used to disregard workers' qualifications and skills, particularly when they had comparable skills and responsibilities, he added.
Ramanan questioned why a graduate qualified to work as a financial manager in Kuala Lumpur should receive RM8,000 while someone doing the same job in Perlis or Terengganu would be eligible for only RM2,500.
He said workers who had studied hard, obtained qualifications and developed their skills deserved fair treatment.
2027 Budget proposed a starting basic salary of RM2,500 for graduates and semi-skilled workers.
The ministry is preparing Starting Basic Salary Guidelines based on job categories under the Malaysia Standard Classification of Occupations, while the implementation mechanism is still being refined.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Penang Port becomes Malaysia's first port with private 5G network
Article:
BUTTERWORTH: Penang Port Sdn Bhd (Penang Port) has become Malaysia's first port to deploy a private 5G network on dedicated spectrum, marking a significant milestone in its digital transformation toward becoming a smart port.
The network, deployed by Altel Communications Sdn Bhd (Altel), covers the North Butterworth Container Terminal (NBCT) and Butterworth Deep Water Wharves (BDWW), spanning approximately 2.5sqkm.
Penang Port acting chief executive officer Fakhrul Azhar Tajudin said the network operates independently of the public commercial mobile network, with its 5G core and associated port applications hosted entirely within the port's premises.
He said this gives the port operator greater control over network performance and operational data, while supporting data sovereignty, security, and low-latency communications.
"The implementation of a private 5G network represents a significant strategic step in realising this vision, enabling the adoption of smart technologies, interconnected systems and progressive automation across the entire port ecosystem," he said at the Penang Port Private 5G Launch ceremony at NBCT today.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil launched the network, with Penang Deputy Chief Minister II Jagdeep Singh Deo; Ministry of Communications deputy secretary general, Telecommunications Infrastructure, V Mano; and Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) managing director Abdul Karim Fakir Ali also in attendance.
Fakhrul Azhar said digital transformation was central to the port's strategy to develop more efficient, resilient and future-ready operations.
The infrastructure is designed to support future adoption of smart port technology, including autonomous prime movers, remote-controlled cranes and gantries, artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled video analytics, and intelligent surveillance systems.
It can also support applications requiring high network availability and latency below 15 milliseconds.
Meanwhile, Altel Group Sdn Bhd Group chief executive officer Dr Afizulazha Abdullah said enterprise digitalisation would increasingly depend on reliable connectivity infrastructure as automation, real-time applications and AI became more integral to operations.
He said private 5G, supported by dedicated spectrum, gives enterprises greater control over connectivity and enables them to develop digital capabilities tailored to their operational requirements.
"This is where private 5G, supported by dedicated spectrum, becomes increasingly relevant. It gives enterprises greater control over their connectivity and the ability to build digital capabilities around their specific operational requirements.
"Penang Port demonstrates how this approach can create the conditions for smarter operations and stronger business outcomes," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fahmi: Communications, Transport ministries to expand 5G coverage at major ports
Article:
BUTTERWORTH: The Communications Ministry will collaborate with the Transport Ministry to expand 5G network coverage across major ports nationwide.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the collaboration builds on previous joint efforts with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) to resolve internet connectivity issues along main Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB) rail routes.
"Previously, the Communications Ministry and MCMC assisted in resolving internet coverage issues along major rail lines. We have identified several areas along the KTMB network from north to south of the Peninsula that still lack satisfactory internet coverage.
"Based on that collaboration, I believe we can expand the deployment of 5G technology, particularly at other ports," he said after launching the Penang Port Private 5G network at Wharf N2, North Butterworth Container Terminal, here today.
Fahmi said a cabinet note will be prepared to enable detailed joint planning between both ministries for this purpose.
He said the successful implementation of the private 5G network at Penang Port demonstrates the technology's capacity to boost productivity, reduce operational costs, and enhance safety through remotely controlled heavy machinery, digital communication systems, and surveillance robots.
"Given that MMC Port Holdings Bhd (MMC Ports) operates several major ports in the country, this technology should be expanded to other ports to accelerate the digital transformation of the national logistics sector," he said.
Fahmi added that Malaysia will propose a review of the international Coverage of Populated Areas metric currently used to measure telecommunication network coverage.
He said the proposal will be presented for consideration at the International Telecommunication Union forum in Doha, Qatar, this November.
He noted that the current metric measures coverage only in populated areas, whereas economic hubs such as ports, rail networks, and major highways also require high-performance connectivity to support 5G deployment.
"I will request the ministry and MCMC to examine whether we should propose expanding this metric beyond populated areas to include locations with critical economic activity," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Perak studying elephant food bank proposal
Article:
IPOH: The state government is studying a proposal to establish an elephant food bank to mitigate human-elephant conflict.
State Science, Environment and Green Technology Committee chairman Teh Kok Lim said the proposal could involve creating buffer zones within elephants' roaming areas to provide them with an alternative food source.
He said the Forestry Department and the Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) would need to work together to identify suitable locations for the initiative.
"We are currently studying the possibility of establishing a food bank for elephants.
"Perhaps we could create buffer zones within the areas where they roam, so they can remain there," he said after attending the state-level Environment and Ozone Day celebrations at Angsana Mall today.
Teh said the proposal was being considered amid concerns over the growing elephant population and shrinking natural habitats.
He added that seasonal changes, particularly during the fruiting season, could influence the animals' movements and increase the likelihood of them venturing into areas used by humans.
"Sometimes, it depends on the season. When the fruiting season arrives, that is when the situation becomes worrying," he said.
However, Teh acknowledged that the approach might not always be effective, as elephants could be difficult to keep within designated areas.
"No matter what food you provide, they may not want it. They prefer to roam freely," he said.
He said the proposal remained under study, with the relevant departments expected to assess its feasibility before any decision was made.
Asked about potential locations for the food bank, Teh said discussions were ongoing to identify suitable sites.
Currently, Perak has no elephant food bank. Such facilities are available in Terengganu, Pahang, Johor and Kelantan.
On the threat posed by wild elephants to fruit orchards in Bukit Bangkong, Chemor, which have been raided three times within weeks, Teh said action would be taken to assist the affected farmers.
"Action will be taken and we believe the elephants are roaming in search of food as the fruiting season approaches," he said.
Yesterday, the New Straits Times reported that the
elephants
were first spotted in the area on Sept 27 before returning on Oct 3 and Oct 11, damaging fruit trees, water tanks, pipes and ponds.
The Bukit Bangkong Hulu Cemor farmers' group said the repeated incursions had raised concerns among orchard owners, who had invested considerable time, effort and money in developing their land.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Taxi drivers thank government, say RM1,000 aid eases burden
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Taxi drivers in the state have thanked the government for a one-off RM1,000 cash assistance, saying it will help cover vehicle maintenance, daily expenses, and family needs.
For veteran drivers, the financial aid provides much-needed relief amid rising operating costs and declining tourist numbers, with several calling for more affordable replacement vehicles to support their livelihoods.
Taxi driver Mohamad Zahir Abd Razak, 55, who has been driving a taxi for more than 15 years, said the aid would help ease the burden of meeting daily expenses, maintaining his vehicle and supporting his children.
"We are very grateful for the RM1,000 assistance. At least, it helps ease the burden of our daily expenses, maintenance and spending on our children," he said after receiving the voucher from Transport Minister Anthony Loke at a ceremony in Dewan Sri Pinang.
Nearly 700 drivers attended the ceremony in Penang, which served as the first distribution event held outside Putrajaya.
The assistance, introduced under the 2027 Budget, will
benefit
about 38,000 taxi and rental car drivers and 15,000 school bus drivers nationwide.
Zahir noted that the government has previously extended support to taxi operators and expressed appreciation for the continued assistance.
Nur Marina Mohamed Elias, in her 50s, who has worked as a driver for 12 years, said she plans to use the money to upgrade her vehicle.
[[nid:1557464]]
She noted that fewer tourist arrivals have impacted daily earnings, making additional financial support crucial for operators facing economic pressure.
Meanwhile, Penang Sentral taxi driver S. Kumaran, 54, said the funds would help support his family, including his 12-year-old child.
He said the money would be useful not only for family expenses during Deepavali but also for his child's schooling next year.
However, Kumaran urged the Transport Ministry to consider making more affordable taxis available to drivers who could not afford pricier models.
He said budget-friendly options would enable drivers to replace ageing vehicles without incurring excessive financial hardship.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Family wants death in custody reclassified as murder
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A group of 80 people, including family members of a man who died in police custody, gathered at Bukit Aman today to submit a memorandum demanding the case be investigated as murder.
The memorandum, supported by dozens of non-governmental organisations including Lawyers for Liberty (LFL) and Amnesty International Malaysia, urged police to reclassify the case under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
LFL lawyers representing the family said Noorizwan Zulkefly, 42, was arrested on Sept 20 and held at the Cheras police headquarters for 11 days. His family claimed they were never informed of his arrest or detention.
"On the night of Sept 30 at 9.30pm, Noorizwan was taken to Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz (HCTM), Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM), in critical condition before being pronounced dead at 1.52am on Oct 1.
"The deceased's sister, Nooranis Zulkefly, only learned of his death at 8pm on Oct 1 via a WhatsApp message from a police officer, approximately 18 hours after his passing.
"Nooranis lodged two police reports on Oct 2 and 3 requesting a full investigation," an LFL representative told reporters outside Bukit Aman.
The family said a senior forensic pathologist at HCTM UKM informed them on Oct 12 that the cause of death was blunt force trauma to the head.
The post-mortem revealed extensive injuries across the body, including severe skull swelling, brain haemorrhage, injuries around the eyes and ears, internal intestinal bleeding, and soft tissue damage to his limbs, chest, back, and hips.
The family claimed that no official explanation has been provided regarding his condition during detention or the origin of his injuries, adding that requests for information from Bukit Aman senior investigating officers were rejected.
The memorandum demands the preservation of all evidence, including lockup closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage, lockup diaries, detention records, and medical files, as well as regular transparent updates on the progress of the investigation.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Fadil Marsus previously maintained that Noorizwan's arrest and detention followed standard operating procedures.
He said the case is being
investigated
by Bukit Aman's Criminal Investigation Unit on Deaths in Custody (USJKT) in collaboration with the Integrity and Standards Compliance Department (JIPS).
LFL lawyer N. Surendran had earlier urged police to classify the death as murder, pointing out the severe physical injuries and the 18-hour delay in notifying the family.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'We have better things to do than set up khalwat traps' – Amirudin
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: PKR has denied allegations that the party is weaponising khalwat (close proximity) claims against rival political leaders to weaken opponents.
PKR vice-president Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari emphasised that PKR does not use personal issues as a basis for political rivalry.
"We have better things to do than set up khalwat traps.
"It has never been discussed or arranged, either secretly or openly, to trap political opponents. That is not our style," he said after officiating the Majlis Semarak Kasih with Yayasan Selangor students here today.
Yesterday, the Selangor Islamic Religious Department detained a former minister and political leader for alleged khalwat with a woman, believed to be the founder of a non-governmental organisation, in Petaling Jaya.
Earlier today, Bersama co-founder Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad admitted to being one of two people detained by the department on suspicion of khalwat (close proximity) on Oct 15, saying he regretted his lapse in judgment.
He said that he was with a woman when
Jais officers
arrived at the location.
Nik Nazmi apologised to his wife, family and everyone affected by his lapse in judgment during the incident. He added that he would fully cooperate with any legal process.
Meanwhile, commenting on preparations for the Melaka election, Amirudin, who is also Pakatan Harapan election strategy director, said PH is finalising several decisions.
"I believe within a week we will set a clearer direction for the election. We will offer good candidates, who are currently in the final screening stages," he said.
Responding to questions on candidate selection for the Melaka polls, Amirudin said the party will field individuals dedicated to community service and equipped with experience.
"In some areas, we want to allow candidates to gain experience, particularly in seats where baseline support may be lower. That will provide a long-term plan for the party and the PH coalition," he said.
Addressing potential cooperation with Bersatu, Amirudin noted that discussions have not been finalised and a decision will be reached soon.
PKR had previously confirmed that it would contest nine seats in the Melaka state election.
Its secretary-general, Fuziah Salleh, said PH would contest more seats overall if PKR fielded candidates in nine constituencies.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze: Childcare centres remain open, outdoor activities suspended
Article:
KUCHING: No childcare centres (taska) have been ordered to close so far due to the haze, but all outdoor activities must be suspended to reduce children's exposure to polluted air.
Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the decision not to order a blanket closure of childcare centres takes into account the needs of working parents who rely on these services.
She said parents have the discretion to decide whether to send their children to taska, particularly in areas where schools have been ordered to close following high Air Pollutant Index (API) readings.
"We understand that some parents cannot simply leave their children at home because there is no one to look after them.
"Parents can discuss with their employers or childcare centre operators on the steps to take. However, the main requirement is that children must not be allowed to play outdoors," she told reporters on the sidelines of the Empowerus 2026 launch in Kuching today.
Nancy also advised parents to take their children for medical check-ups if they show symptoms of illness while the haze persists.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RM1,000 aid to ease cost pressures on taxi, rental car drivers
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The government is stepping up efforts to help taxi and rental car drivers cope with rising operating costs and stiff competition, including a one-off RM1,000 aid for eligible drivers nationwide.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said the government recognised the challenges faced by drivers, particularly rising spare parts prices and the cost of living, and was pursuing further measures to support the industry.
"We know taxi drivers face various challenges, including rising vehicle spare parts costs and the cost of living.
"While RM1,000 may not solve all their problems, at least it can help ease their financial burden," he said at the one-off aid distribution ceremony held at Dewan Sri Pinang today.
The
assistance
, introduced under the 2027 Budget, will benefit about 38,000 taxi and rental car drivers and 15,000 school bus drivers nationwide.
Loke said the government had decided to distribute the aid immediately, without waiting for the Budget to be passed, following a directive from Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said the initiative was funded by RM91 million raised through the auction of special vehicle registration numbers beginning with the letter H, traditionally associated with taxis.
Nearly 700 drivers attended the ceremony in Penang, the first distribution event outside Putrajaya.
Recipients received Bank Simpanan Nasional vouchers redeemable for RM1,000 in cash from Monday.
Those who did not receive vouchers would have the money transferred into their bank accounts within one to two weeks.
Eligible drivers must hold valid driver's cards, with no additional application required.
Loke said the Transport Ministry was also working with Proton to help drivers replace ageing vehicles through a financing scheme, with measures to reduce costs and financing from Aeon Bank at reasonable rates.
He urged drivers to upgrade their vehicles where possible and improve safety, comfort and service standards to remain competitive and maintain passenger confidence.
Penang's growing tourism sector could offer further opportunities, he said, with the expansion of Penang International Airport expected to increase annual passenger capacity from 6.5 million to 12 million upon completion.
Loke said the government hoped the cash assistance and longer-term initiatives would help drivers manage immediate financial pressures while strengthening the industry's competitiveness.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ministry studying Mediation Act amendments
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The National Unity Ministry (KPN) is reviewing proposed improvements to the Mediation Act 2012 to establish a clearer legal framework for strengthening community mediation services under the National Unity and Integration Department (JPNIN).
Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang said the Act, which falls under the Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU), does not specifically cover the operation of JPNIN's community mediation services.
He said JPNIN's mediation services, including training and accreditation for community mediators, were currently based on Section 8(d) of the Rukun Tetangga Act 2012.
However, the provision was insufficient to establish a comprehensive legal framework for the services.
"I have therefore asked JPNIN to meet with BHEUU to review the proposed improvements, including amendments to the Mediation Act 2012, to provide a clearer legal basis for these services," he said.
He was speaking at the launch of the Seri Kota Public Housing Collaborative Social Project on Community Mediation here today.
Also present was Bandar Tun Razak Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, the Prime Minister's wife.
Aaron also called on JPNIN and the National Integration Research and Training Institute (IKLIN) to conduct comparative studies of countries with specific legal frameworks for community mediation, including Singapore, India and Sri Lanka.
He cited Singapore's Community Mediation Centres Act 1997, India's Mediation Act 2023 and Sri Lanka's Mediation Boards Act 1988 as examples for comparison.
The study, he said, would help assess how legislation in these countries regulates the powers and functions of mediation bodies, mediator accreditation, mediation procedures and safeguards for parties involved.
Meanwhile, the government will expand its network of Community Mediation Centres by establishing 12 new centres at strategic locations nationwide this year, including in Kota Kinabalu, Sabah; Miri, Sarawak; Pontian, Johor; Kuala Terengganu, Terengganu; and Shah Alam, Selangor.
"These centres will serve as community reference points for information, preliminary advice and appropriate channels to resolve community issues and disputes.
"This approach will help identify and address conflicts early, before they escalate into more serious disputes and strain community relations," he said.
On the Seri Kota Public Housing Community Mediation Centre, Aaron said it was JPNIN's 11th such centre.
Its location was selected based on several factors, including a population of nearly 6,000, available local facilities, community demand and the need to address neighbourhood issues.
He said the centre's establishment also followed a resolution proposed at the 2024 K2K Initiative Development Strategic Workshop organised by Think City in collaboration with government agencies and stakeholders. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesian fisherman found safe after 9 days adrift at sea
Article:
KUANTAN: An Indonesian fisherman who went missing after his boat lost contact at sea was found safe near Pulau Tioman on Oct 15, nine days after departing from Indonesia.
The fisherman, identified as Bachtiar, 61, was found by the public about 22 nautical miles east of the island.
Pahang Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency director First Admiral Datuk Mazlan Mat Rejab said the boat had departed from Letung in Indonesia's Anambas Islands Regency on Oct 6 before contact was lost.
"The Maritime Rescue Sub-Centre (MRSC) in Kuantan received information about the missing boat from its Indonesian counterpart via email on Oct 14. The Johor Baru MRSC subsequently informed us that the boat had been spotted by members of the public on Oct 15.
"The MMEA then deployed its Perkasa 1246 boat to the location near Pulau Tioman. The fisherman was brought to the island at 3.10am yesterday and taken to the Tekek Health Clinic for a medical check-up," he said in a statement today.
He said investigations revealed that the fisherman had lost contact after his boat ran out of fuel, leaving it adrift at sea.
He said the agency had contacted the Indonesian Consulate to inform it of the discovery and coordinate arrangements, including the necessary documentation and the fisherman's return to Indonesia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SAR operation underway for father, son feared lost in Besut forest
Article:
JERTIH: A man and his son are feared lost in a forest near the La Hot Spring recreational area in Hulu Besut after going there to look for medicinal roots on Thursday, and police are tracking them based on a location alert sent by the son.
Besut district chief Supt Mohd Rozaime Ab Rahim said the Search And Rescue (SAR) operation resumed at 8am, involving 38 personnel from various agencies and local villagers.
He said the search team received information that Adam Adnan, 25, had managed to contact his family at about 10 am today and share their last known location in the forest.
"Based on the location provided by the man, the rescue team proceeded to the area to locate the two men and bring them out," he told reporters here today.
The operation involves personnel from the Police, Fire and Rescue Department, Civil Defence Force and villagers.
Mohd Rozaime said police received a missing persons report from the wife of one of the men yesterday, prompting the search operation.
Adam's wife, Nur Aliah Zamin, 20, said her husband and father-in-law, Adnan Mohamad, 57, had entered the forest to look for roots believed to be intended to treat her father-in-law's nerve problems.
She said the two men, who are from Kulim, Kedah, arrived in the area on Wednesday for the search and a holiday.
Nur Aliah said her husband worked as a stall assistant in Kulim, while her father-in-law was unemployed.
The family was also informed that the two men had not taken any food supplies with them into the forest, raising concerns about their condition. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thunderstorm, heavy rain warning in 9 states until 3pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm, heavy rain and strong winds warning for nine states until 3pm today.
In a statement, MetMalaysia said the warning covers Bandar Baharu and Kulim in Kedah, the whole of Penang, and several districts in Perak, namely Selama, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Muallim, Kinta, Kampar and Batang Padang.
The same conditions are also expected in Terengganu, covering Kemaman and Dungun, and Pahang, involving Bentong, Jerantut, Kuantan, Maran, Rompin, Pekan, Raub, Cameron Highlands and Lipis.
In Selangor, the affected areas are Hulu Selangor, Gombak and Hulu Langat, while in Negri Sembilan, they are Seremban and Jelebu. In Johor, the warning covers Pontian, Kota Tinggi, Kulai, Mersing, Segamat and Johor Baru.
In Sarawak, the affected areas are Betong (Kabong and Saratok), Sibu, Kapit (Song), Sarikei and Mukah.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Laos drug jet case on agenda at Malaysia-Philippines meeting in Sabah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian police will raise the seizure of 521kg of crystal methamphetamine from a private jet in Laos during a meeting with their Philippine counterparts in Kota Kinabalu, Sabah, next week.
Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the meeting with the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) had been arranged before the Oct 1 seizure at Luang Prabang International Airport.
He said the meeting was initially scheduled to discuss regional drug trafficking issues, but Malaysian authorities would now use the opportunity to exchange information on the syndicate believed to be behind the private jet case.
"The meeting had been scheduled before the private jet was detained in Laos.
"We plan to discuss the issue with our counterparts at this meeting," he told the New Straits Times.
Hussein said Malaysian police had already shared intelligence with Philippine authorities to help identify those behind the international drug trafficking operation.
"We have shared our intelligence with them. PDEA and the Philippine National Police (PNP) are working on identifying the syndicate there," he said.
The meeting comes as investigators continue efforts to establish the full extent of the trafficking network, which is believed to have links spanning Malaysia, Laos and the Philippines.
When asked whether NCID officers had received clearance from Lao authorities to travel there for follow-up investigations, Hussein said approval had yet to be granted.
He said Malaysian police were still awaiting clearance to conduct investigations in Laos following the arrest of a Malaysian second officer, or co-pilot, in connection with the seizure.
On Oct 1, Lao authorities seized
crystal methamphetamine
from a private jet at Luang Prabang International Airport and detained 13 people, including a Malaysian crew member.
Investigations revealed that the aircraft had earlier departed Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport in Subang for Laos without carrying any cargo.
The jet was believed to have been intended to transport the drugs from Laos to Manila in the Philippines.
Police had earlier disclosed that the charter flight was arranged by an individual believed to be from the Philippines for US$49,500 (about RM209,000).
The shipment was declared as "goods" for transportation from Laos to the Philippines.
Investigators believed the
mastermind
behind the trafficking operation was a Filipino.
He said intelligence had been shared with PDEA to help trace and apprehend the person.
Malaysian police have also investigated individuals and aviation companies linked to the aircraft.
On Oct 7, a police operation involving the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) and aviation security personnel was conducted at a hangar in Subang.
A 49-year-old Malaysian pilot who owned an aviation company linked to the jet involved in the Laos seizure was among those arrested.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fadhlina: Police handling probe into suspicious packages at schools
Article:
MELAKA: The Education Ministry is leaving the investigation into suspicious packages found at nine schools in Negri Sembilan to the police, says Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek.
She said the ministry remained vigilant about suspicious items found at schools nationwide and stressed the importance of prioritising school safety.
"We urge all principals, headmasters, and school personnel to remain vigilant and prepared, especially when it comes to matters involving school safety.
"Once again, we would like to thank the police for ensuring that all aspects of security are given priority," she said after officiating the 'Fadhlina Membaca' Women's Reading Club with the Education Minister here today.
Yesterday, Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad confirmed police received nine reports concerning suspicious packages found at several schools in Nilai and Tampin.
Alzafny said inspections revealed all the boxes contained wheat flour and plastic plates.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Penang unveils Silicon Island Experience Centre as reclamation hits 200ha
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Penang has reached a significant milestone in the Silicon Island project, with Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow making his first vehicular visit to the island and launching the Silicon Island Experience Centre today.
He said the mega development would serve as a major catalyst for the state's economic growth over the next 50 years.
"Silicon Island is not just another reclamation project, but a strategic catalyst for the state's economic growth for the next 50 years," he said during the visit.
Chow said the project built on Penang's 50-year legacy in the semiconductor industry by introducing high-value manufacturing, research and development, and artificial intelligence capabilities.
He reaffirmed the state government's commitment to low-carbon development through the 280ha Green Tech Park and the 5-Diamond Low Carbon City Framework, while continuing to support local fishermen through financial assistance and community programmes.
Speaking at the launch, state Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the Experience Centre served as a crucial link between the master plan and its physical implementation.
He highlighted key infrastructure components, including the Pan Island Link 2A (PIL2A) bridge connecting Permatang Damar Laut directly to
Silicon Island
, which is designed to ensure smooth logistics and transport integration.
"The state government's commitment goes beyond building roads and bridges. Silicon Island is designed for the future, with sustainable transport, smart traffic systems, integrated pedestrian and bicycle lanes, and resilient digital infrastructure," he said.
Penang Infrastructure Corporation chief executive officer Datuk Seri Farizan Darus said the 2,500sqft facility was completed in four months at a cost of RM2.5 million.
It features an advanced LED scale model controlled via an iPad, offering interactive views of the 920ha master plan, including infrastructure networks, 160.8ha of dedicated green spaces and marine conservation zones.
Farizan said physical land reclamation at the site had reached 200ha.
Work on the RM420 million PIL2A contract was progressing smoothly, with the first phase featuring a 1.5km marine bridge scheduled to open its first section by December 2028, ahead of full completion in June 2029.
He added that more than RM30 million had been disbursed to local fishermen under the Social Impact Management Plan (SIMP), alongside ongoing ecological mitigation projects.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sister tells young nieces mother died of illness, withholds murder details
Article:
TUMPAT: The elder sister of Norhazwani Ibrahim, 35, told her two young nieces this morning that their mother had died, but withheld details of her death after she was found murdered at government quarters in Jalan Kuarters KLIA, Nilai, Negri Sembilan, on Thursday.
Marliza Ibrahim, 48, said she told the children, aged five and six, that their mother had died of an illness rather than reveal the circumstances of her death.
"When they asked why, I simply told them she was sick," she said.
"I could not bring myself to tell them the actual incident, as they are too young to understand," she said when contacted today.
Marliza added that their family home in Kampung Banjir, Telaga Lanas, continues to receive visitors, including friends of the deceased.
She said a post-mortem was conducted this morning, and the remains will be brought back to their hometown for burial at the Tanjung Islamic Cemetery in Pengkalan Kubor immediately upon arrival.
Norhazwani was a Customs Officer who transferred to the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency scheme and was stationed at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA).
It was previously reported that she was allegedly
stabbed to death
by her husband at their home in the KLIA quarters in Nilai.
The victim suffered two stab wounds to the left abdomen and one to the right cheek. The suspect surrendered to police shortly after the incident and has been remanded for seven days starting yesterday to assist investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze triggers highest alert level in southern Asean region
Article:
SINGAPORE: Ongoing fires in Indonesia that have blanketed parts of Southeast Asia with toxic haze have triggered the highest-level alert by the regional bloc's climate and fire monitor.
"Activation of Alert Level 3 for the Southern Asean region," the Singapore Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre said on its website, seen on Saturday.
Based near Singapore's Changi Airport, the ASMC uses a four-tiered alert level system, from zero to three, with the highest triggered if there is a "high risk of severe transboundary haze in the region."
This included significant and persistent hotspot activities with widespread moderate to dense smoke haze, observed over two or more consecutive days, dry weather persisting and wind continuing to blow haze towards neighbouring Asean countries.
The ASMC alert was issued Friday, but similar alerts have already been handed out twice this year – on Aug 26 and March 27.
The months-long spell of haze has been disrupting life in large parts of Southeast Asia, closing schools and spiking respiratory complaints.
Singapore said on Friday it would issue warnings to seven companies in Indonesia it identified as responsible for fires but warned the worst may yet to come.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia Airlines resumes Jeddah, Madinah flights tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Airlines will resume scheduled flights to and from Jeddah and Madinah tomorrow.
Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) said the decision follows a comprehensive safety review and operational risk assessment after temporary suspensions triggered by security concerns in Saudi Arabia.
"Passengers travelling to and from both destinations from Oct 18 should verify their flight schedules and ensure their contact details are updated through the 'My Booking' section on its website or mobile app.
"Passengers who booked through third-party platforms or travel agents should contact their respective providers directly to confirm their travel arrangements.
"For assistance, passengers can use the airline's Live Chat service or contact its Global Contact Centre at 1 300 88 3000 within Malaysia or +603 7843 3000 from overseas," it said in a statement.
The airline also said that it would continue to monitor developments in the region as the safety and security of its passengers and crew remain its highest priority.
It was reported that Malaysia Airlines had cancelled flights between Kuala Lumpur and Jeddah and Madinah from Oct 12 to 17 following reported Houthi missile attacks on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Children must not be stigmatised over birth status - Minister
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The public has been reminded not to use a child's 'nasab' (birth or lineage) status as a reason to insult, shame or discriminate against them, forcing them to bear a social burden throughout their lives.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said a child should not be blamed for the circumstances of their birth, as Islamic principles clearly state that no individual bears the sins of another.
He said that while legal rulings concerning lineage must be upheld, they should not be used as an excuse to subject children to social judgement.
"Discussions on legal rulings should not be used as a reason to insult, shame or discriminate against a child.
"We need to build a society that can distinguish between evaluating an act and condemning a person for the rest of their life," he said when delivering his speech at the 'Seminar Nasab Kebangsaan: Dinamika Cabaran Keluarga Kosmopolitan (SANAD) 2026', organised by Persatuan Kebajikan Bayt Al-Rahmah, today.
Zulkifli said society should also be mindful of the language used within families, educational institutions and administrative settings to avoid causing children to bear a prolonged social stigma.
He said the Quranic principle that no individual bears the sins of another should serve as a moral foundation for ensuring that children are not blamed for the circumstances of their birth.
Meanwhile, Zulkifli said due attention should be given to mothers facing pregnancy or childbirth crises, as they might need assistance in accessing healthcare services, continuing their education and rebuilding their emotional stability.
"They may need support in accessing healthcare services, continuing their education, rebuilding their emotional stability, improving family relationships or planning their future more systematically," he said.
On the matter of lineage, Zulkifli said it should not be addressed based solely on assumptions, public perceptions or emotions, but required careful examination of the facts, an understanding of syariah principles and consultation with the relevant authorities.
He said the issue also had implications for family matters, inheritance, guardianship, mahram relationships, as well as the naming and registration of births, all of which needed to be examined in accordance with the relevant religious rulings and legal provisions.
He said the management of lineage-related issues should not stop at determining the legal status alone, as attention must also be given to the child's care, education, protection, well-being and future.
In this regard, he stressed the importance of integrated cooperation among religious institutions, courts, government agencies, welfare organisations, counselling service providers and non-governmental organisations (NGOs) in addressing challenges related to lineage.
"Lineage issues cannot be understood from just one perspective. They require scholarly examination, an understanding of syariah principles, accuracy in legal and administrative matters, as well as concern for the impact on individuals and families," he said.
Zulkifli said NGOs and shelters also played an important role in identifying gaps in support and unmet needs among mothers and children.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bersama suspends Nik Nazmi from party activities for three months from Oct 20 after Jais incident
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — Parti Bersama Malaysia has suspended Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad from all official party activities for three months, effective October 20.
The party said the decision followed his public admission regarding his involvement in an incident with the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais) in Petaling Jaya on October 15.
In his earlier statement, Nik Nazmi
confirmed
he was the man caught with a woman, who is not his
muhrim
(a legally permissible close relative), in an enclosed space during the raid, and publicly apologised to his wife, family and party members.
“Bersama views this development seriously and takes the position that every issue involving the party’s leadership and members must be addressed appropriately to preserve the party’s integrity, credibility and public confidence,” Syukri Razab said in a statement on behalf of the party.
The suspension will run until January 19, 2027.
The party stated that the decision was necessary and reasonable, without denying Nik Nazmi’s contributions and commitment to Bersama since the party was relaunched in May 2026.

Title: Drug abuse among Malaysian under-15s a growing concern, says Saifuddin Nasution
Article:
MACHANG, Oct 17 — The trend of drug abuse among those under the age of 15 is increasingly concerning and requires more comprehensive preventive efforts, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said that based on the profiles of individuals involved in drug abuse, those aged between 15 and 39 formed the largest group.
He added that this development necessitates a preventive approach that also emphasises early education and the role of parents in curbing the involvement of youngsters in drug abuse.
“The National Anti-Drugs Agency (AADK) has three main functions, namely education and prevention, enforcement and rehabilitation, to address the issue of drug abuse.
“Efforts to educate the public must be strengthened to raise awareness and encourage preventive action among families,” he told a media conference after attending the Home Ministry’s Madani Adopted Village and Madani Adopted School 2026 launching ceremony here today.
Meanwhile, commenting on the seizure of 521 kilogrammes (kg) of methamphetamine from a private jet in Laos recently, Saifuddin Nasution said the drugs were found aboard the aircraft before it was due to depart for Manila.
He said the aircraft had departed from Subang for Laos without any drugs on board, before the consignment was loaded into the plane when it was in that country.
“Laotian authorities detected the drugs when the aircraft was about to continue its flight to Manila,.
“Police have traced the aircraft’s owner, as well as its pilot and co-pilot, to assist in the investigation as the aircraft had departed from Subang,” he said.
He said investigation was also focusing on the party that charted the aircraft, the purpose of the charter and its intended destination.
Saifuddin Nasution said the aircraft owner’s identity had been established, but further details of the investigation could not yet be disclosed.
Previously, Lao police seized 521kg of crystal methamphetamine from a private Learjet that had arrived from Malaysia at Luang Prabang International Airport, with 13 individuals arrested in connection with the case.
The Vientiane Times, quoting the Lao Security Newspaper, reported that the security operation was conducted on October 1 following information received by provincial police on Sept 21 regarding a drug trafficking syndicate believed to be planning to smuggle narcotics across the border by air, using a private aircraft.
According to the report, police subsequently received information about a change in the flight schedule, with the private jet expected to arrive from Malaysia at Luang Prabang International Airport at 1.30 pm on October 1. — Bernama

Title: Lawyer: Zara Qairina’s mother yet to decide on civil action as inquest nears conclusion
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 17 — The legal team representing Noraidah Lamat, the mother of Zara Qairina Mahathir, has yet to decide whether to pursue civil action against any party, with its immediate focus on completing written submissions for the inquest.
Counsel Shahlan Jufri, speaking on behalf of the team, said the matter would be discussed with Noraidah before any decision was made on further legal action.
“For now, our focus is on the inquest, particularly the written submissions. We will discuss the matter with our client, as the final decision on whether to take civil action against any party deemed responsible rests with her,” he told a press conference after the inquest proceedings yesterday.
Shahlan also revealed that Noraidah had sent a brief WhatsApp message that morning, expressing her hope that everything would be made easier.
He thanked members of the media for their coverage of the inquest, describing it as professional, accurate and timely.
Shahlan said the 96-day inquest had been a challenging process, although it had proceeded relatively swiftly alongside proceedings in the Court for Children.
“There is a lot that we need to address in our written submissions, and we hope the decision eventually reached will be fair to all parties,” he said.
On the funds raised to support the inquest, Shahlan clarified that the amount collected was slightly more than RM200,000, dismissing claims that it had reached RM1 million or RM2 million.
He said the fund was announced by Senator Marhamah Rosli last year and had been independently audited after Noraidah and the legal team appointed a qualified independent accountant in April this year.
According to Shahlan, the money was intended solely to cover expenses related to the inquest and had not been used for other purposes.
He added that the legal team had handled the case on a pro bono basis, meaning no legal fees were charged.
Shahlan also said there was no legal requirement for Noraidah or the legal team to make the audit report publicly available. — Daily Express

Title: Man loses RM363,887 in alleged fake bank auction property scam in Miri
Article:
MIRI, Oct 17 — A man who intended to buy a property for his family has allegedly been cheated out of RM363,887.49 in a non-existent bank auction property deal.
Miri District Police Chief ACP Mohd Farhan Lee Abdullah said in a statement shared on Miri police’s official social media page that the 56-year-old victim lodged a police report at Miri Central Police Station on October 15.
According to the police report, the victim had known the suspect for about two years through business dealings and friendship.
“In November 2025, the complainant intended to purchase a house for family use in Kuching. The suspect then allegedly offered five houses in the Taman Abadi area, Kuching, which were claimed to be bank auction houses at prices lower than the market rate.
“The suspect also offered to manage the purchase process, including the preparation of the Sales and Purchase Agreement (SPA) and property title transfer,” said the statement.
Mohd Farhan said the complainant claimed to have made several payments in stages between November 2025 and January 2026 for the proposed purchases, including deposits, land surveying fees and payments related to the Inland Revenue Board (LHDN).
“However, the purchase arrangements were allegedly not completed as promised. The complainant also claimed that they have yet to receive complete documents proving ownership of the houses, despite contacting the suspect repeatedly for clarification,” he said.
Police are investigating the case under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating and dishonestly inducing the delivery of property.
Police advised the public to be cautious of property offers at unrealistically low prices, verify property status through official channels, consult qualified lawyers and avoid transferring money to third-party accounts without proper verification. — The Borneo Post

Title: Transport minister: RM1,000 aid for remaining eligible taxi, rental car and school bus drivers to be paid via EFT
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 17 — The remaining eligible taxi, rental car and school bus drivers nationwide will receive the RM1,000 Special Financial Aid directly into their respective bank accounts through Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT).
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said the disbursement through this method would be carried out in the next phase, following the first phase of direct handovers to eligible drivers in several zones.
He said that in the first phase, the aid would be handed directly to eligible recipients in selected zones, with Penang hosting the second presentation ceremony after the launch in Putrajaya on October 14.
“For the second ceremony, we are very pleased to be able to bring together 700 taxi and rental car drivers in Penang, who were selected as symbolic representatives to receive the aid in person.
“All the aid will be handed over to those who have been verified as eligible before Deepavali,” he told reporters after the special financial aid presentation ceremony for taxi, rental car and school bus drivers at Dewan Sri Pinang here today.
He also reminded drivers to ensure that they met the eligibility requirements to facilitate the screening of recipient data.
The main requirements include holding a driver card and a valid vehicle licence or permit (VP), as well as a valid Public Service Vehicle (PSV) licence.
Loke also urged drivers to keep abreast of announcements by the Land Public Transport Agency (APAD), the Commercial Vehicle Licensing Board (LPKP) Sabah and LPKP Sarawak regarding the required information and verification process.
He said coordination among agencies under the Transport Ministry was important to ensure that the screening of recipient data was carried out transparently and fairly.
“I know that this RM1,000 may not solve all your problems or fully cover vehicle maintenance costs. However, I sincerely hope this assistance can, to some extent, ease your household expenses, help you replace worn-out tyres or fill your fuel tanks so that you can continue going out to earn a living,” he said.
On October 9, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced a one-off RM1,000 special financial aid for taxi, rental car and school bus drivers as one of the initiatives under Budget 2027. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia records 5,278 domestic violence cases, with numbers still climbing, says Nancy Shukri (VIDEO)
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 17 — A total of 5,278 domestic violence cases have been reported in Malaysia, with the number continuing to rise, said Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri.
She said the ministry was placing greater emphasis on counselling and women’s empowerment to help women better understand their rights, build confidence and achieve financial independence.
“When women are financially independent, they can be more confident in standing up for themselves and are less likely to tolerate abuse,” Nancy told reporters at the EmpowerUS 2026 seminar at the Sarawak State Library here today.
https://www.facebook.com/borneopost.online/videos/a-total-of-5278-domestic-violence-cases-have-been-reported-in-malaysia-with-the-/1385867886638367/
Commenting on the recent case in Negeri Sembilan involving a 35-year-old female customs officer who was allegedly murdered by her husband, Nancy said the ministry was looking into providing assistance to the victim’s family and children.
“We are making preparations to provide assistance, particularly for the children and the family of the victim,” she said, adding that the ministry remained ready to assist families in need.
In July and August, 632 domestic violence cases were recorded in each month, up from 601 in June.
However, the figures remained below the 766 cases recorded in April, the highest monthly total so far in 2026.
Meanwhile, Talian Kasih recorded 104,784 calls as of October 2026, surpassing the 98,050 calls received throughout 2025.
Nancy said the increase in calls indicated growing public awareness of the helpline and the assistance it provides.
“Even children know what to do. It is not just for abuse; it is also for those who are facing problems with their families and need help,” she added. — The Borneo Post

Title: Sarawakian couple allegedly paid three friends RM8,000 each to smuggle cocaine into Japan, says Bukit Aman
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 17 — A Sarawakian husband and wife allegedly recruited three friends to traffic cocaine into Japan, said Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan.
The Star reported that each of the three friends was paid RM8,000 and was believed to have known they were carrying contraband.
“We believe they knew what they were carrying. At the very least, they knew they were carrying something illegal,” he said at a press conference at Johor police headquarters on Friday.
Hussein said the couple had invited their three friends on what was presented as a holiday in Japan.
Each was given a pair of shoes containing concealed drugs before travelling to Kuala Lumpur International Airport for their flight to Tokyo.
The five suspects, all Sarawakians, were arrested at Haneda International Airport in Tokyo last Saturday after Japanese authorities discovered 5kg of cocaine concealed in the insoles of their shoes.
Police have also identified a sixth suspect who managed to return to Malaysia.
None of the five suspects had prior criminal records, and investigations are ongoing to determine whether they had travelled to other countries using the same modus operandi. — The Borneo Post

Title: Slain border agency officer’s remains to be buried in Tumpat tonight, says home minister
Article:
MACHANG, Oct 17 — The remains of a Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency officer allegedly killed by her husband in Nilai, Negeri Sembilan, underwent a post-mortem this morning before being transported to Tumpat, Kelantan, for burial.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the remains were being transported by road and were expected to arrive in Tumpat tonight.
He said the suspect had recently been released from prison after serving a sentence for a drug-related offence.
“The victim leaves behind two children, aged five and six, who are now being cared for by her older sister,” he told a press conference after attending the launch of the Home Ministry’s 2026 Kampung Angkat Madani and Sekolah Angkat Madani initiatives here today.
The officer was found dead last Thursday at the staff quarters of Kuala Lumpur International Airport, in an incident in which she was believed to have been killed by her husband.
Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad reportedly said police received information about the incident at 8.30pm that day.
Meanwhile, Kampung Gosong here has received RM500,000 to upgrade public facilities and residents’ homes under the ministry’s Kampung Angkat Madani initiative.
Saifuddin said the upgrades would cover the mosque, surau, toilets, ablution areas and cemetery, alongside repairs to 14 houses.
He said the house repairs were being carried out in collaboration with Akademi Binaan Malaysia and involved 10 individuals under the supervision of the Prisons Department, as well as members of the People’s Volunteer Corps.
In a related development, Sekolah Kebangsaan Jambul Lawar received RM100,000 under the Sekolah Angkat Madani initiative to upgrade its facilities, including the ceiling, toilets, water supply, computer laboratory and guard post.
The school had also been equipped with smart boards to improve pupils’ interaction during teaching and learning sessions.
In addition, 82 villagers and 54 students received zakat assistance distributed through the corporate zakat wakalah scheme of PBLT Sdn Bhd. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: AKPS stands for Agensi Kawalan dan Perlindungan Sempadan Malaysia, or Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency. KLIA stands for Kuala Lumpur International Airport.
