ABM stands for Akademi Binaan Malaysia, or Malaysian Construction Academy. Rela stands for Ikatan Relawan Rakyat Malaysia, or Malaysia Volunteer Corps.

Title: Ports, railways and highways could be next in Malaysia’s 5G coverage push
Article:
BUTTERWORTH, Oct 17 — The Communications Ministry and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) will study expanding telecommunications coverage targets, particularly for 5G, to include key economic areas such as ports, rail lines and highways.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the current Coverage of Populated Area (CoPA) metric should be reviewed to account for connectivity needs in areas with few or no residents but significant economic activity.
“CoPA is frequently used by telecommunications companies and international bodies to refer to connectivity in populated areas. However, when we talk about 5G access, areas such as ports have no residents but are hubs for significant economic activities,” he said.
He said Malaysia would also raise the issue at international forums, including an International Telecommunication Union (ITU) meeting in Doha in November, to discuss extending 5G and future technologies beyond populated areas to economic hubs.
Fahmi was speaking to reporters after launching the Penang Port Private 5G initiative at the North Butterworth Container Terminal (NBCT) today, making Penang Port the first port in Malaysia to adopt a private 5G network through a collaboration between Altel Communications Sdn Bhd (Altel) and Penang Port.
Also present were Penang Deputy Chief Minister II Jagdeep Singh Deo, Communications Ministry deputy secretary-general for telecommunications infrastructure V. Mano and MCMC managing director Abdul Karim Fakir Ali.
Fahmi said reliable connectivity was essential for industrial operations and that telecommunications infrastructure should not be concentrated solely in populated areas.
Private 5G networks could also be expanded to manufacturing and logistics, particularly for multinational companies (MNCs) operating in Malaysia, he added.
He said the technology offered dedicated connectivity and could support more devices simultaneously, including machinery and equipment requiring high precision.
Fahmi, who is also the Madani government spokesman, said his ministry would prepare a Cabinet memorandum on the proposal and work with the Ministry of Transport (MOT) to extend coverage, including through 5G deployment at other ports.
He cited previous cooperation between the two ministries to address internet connectivity gaps along major rail routes, including sections managed by Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB).
“Based on our previous cooperation with MOT, I believe we can expand these efforts, including by leveraging 5G technology, regardless of who provides the service, for deployment at ports,” he said.
Fahmi said private 5G networks differed from conventional networks by providing dedicated communication channels for critical industrial operations, without requiring users to share network capacity with others.
He said the technology should also be adopted more widely by private-sector operators, including manufacturers and oil palm plantation companies, to improve operational efficiency and safety. — Bernama

Title: Motorists say RON95 wrecked their engines, and Selangor is now investigating seven petrol stations over watery fuel claims
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 17 — Selangor is investigating seven petrol stations after motorists complained that RON95 petrol suspected of being contaminated with water had damaged their vehicle engines, following similar allegations in northern states earlier this month.
Selangor Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry director Muhamad Hanif Asa’ari said the ministry had received 10 official complaints involving the seven premises and collected 27 petrol samples for laboratory analysis.
“Investigations found that consumer complaints involved various symptoms of engine damage, such as abnormal engine noises, jerking, loss of power, engines failing to start and cases of burnt engine valves,” he was quoted by news outlet
Harian Metro
as saying today.
Hanif said some vehicle service centres had confirmed that water contamination in fuel tanks was responsible for engine damage in complainants’ vehicles.
Initial inspections found that all seven stations had valid Special Approval Licences and licences under the Petroleum Development Act 1974.
However, the ministry issued notices requiring the operators to provide relevant documents and information to assist the investigation.
The ministry is investigating possible offences under Section 5(1)(c), read together with Sections 6(1)(d) and 7 of the Trade Descriptions Act 2011, concerning alleged false trade descriptions relating to the content of the petrol supplied.
Hanif urged oil companies and petrol station operators to maintain their underground storage tanks regularly and comply with fuel quality and safety standards.
Motorists who suspect they have been affected were advised to keep their petrol receipts and workshop inspection reports as evidence when lodging complaints with the ministry.
Earlier complaints in northern states
Earlier this month, Penang’s Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry office reported receiving 33 complaints involving about 30 petrol stations over alleged water contamination in RON95.
An inspection at a station in Batu Kawan found no evidence of water contamination.
In Kedah, the ministry collected samples from 11 stations after motorists reported vehicle breakdowns following refuelling.
In Perak, inspections at six stations in Ipoh, Taiping and Kuala Kangsar found no initial signs of water in the storage tanks examined.
Authorities said laboratory results were needed to determine whether the allegations were substantiated.
There is no confirmed evidence currently that the complaints in Selangor and the northern states are connected.

Title: Haze-hit areas: Parents to decide on childcare attendance, but kids must stay indoors, says family minister
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 17 — No
taska
(childcare centres) have been ordered to close so far due to the haze, but all outdoor activities must be suspended to reduce children’s exposure to polluted air.
Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the decision not to order a blanket closure of childcare centres took into account the needs of working parents who rely on the services.
She said parents had the discretion to decide whether to send their children to childcare centres, particularly in areas where schools had been ordered to close following high Air Pollutant Index readings.
“We understand that some parents cannot simply leave their children at home because there is no one to look after them.
“So, perhaps parents can discuss with their employers or the respective childcare centre operators on the steps to be taken. However, the main requirement that must be observed is that children must not be allowed to play outdoors,” she told reporters after officiating the Empowerus 2026, themed ‘Empowering Leaders: Sustainable, Resilient and Ethical Leadership’, here today.
Nancy advised parents to take their children for medical check-ups if they showed symptoms of illness while the haze persisted. — Bernama

Title: From neighbour disputes to legal reform, Malaysia moves to strengthen community mediation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — The Ministry of National Unity (KPN) is reviewing proposed improvements to the Mediation Act 2012 to establish a clearer legal framework for strengthening community mediation services under the National Unity and Integration Department (JPNIN).
Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang said the Act, which falls under the Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU), does not specifically cover the operation of JPNIN’s community mediation services.
He said JPNIN’s mediation services, including training and accreditation for community mediators, were currently based on Section 8(d) of the Rukun Tetangga Act 2012.
However, the provision was insufficient to establish a comprehensive legal framework for the services.
“I have therefore asked JPNIN to meet with BHEUU to review the proposed improvements, including amendments to the Mediation Act 2012, to provide a clearer legal basis for these services,” he said.
He was speaking at the launch of the Seri Kota Public Housing Collaborative Social Project on Community Mediation here today.
Also present was Bandar Tun Razak Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, the prime minister’s wife.
Aaron also called on JPNIN and the National Integration Research and Training Institute (IKLIN) to conduct comparative studies of countries with specific legal frameworks for community mediation, including Singapore, India and Sri Lanka.
He cited Singapore’s Community Mediation Centres Act 1997, India’s Mediation Act 2023 and Sri Lanka’s Mediation Boards Act 1988 as examples for comparison.
The study, he said, would help assess how legislation in these countries regulates the powers and functions of mediation bodies, mediator accreditation, mediation procedures and safeguards for parties involved.
Meanwhile, the government will expand its network of Community Mediation Centres by establishing 12 new centres at strategic locations nationwide this year, including in Kota Kinabalu, Sabah; Miri, Sarawak; Pontian, Johor; Kuala Terengganu, Terengganu; and Shah Alam, Selangor.
“These centres will serve as community reference points for information, preliminary advice and appropriate channels to resolve community issues and disputes.
“This approach will help identify and address conflicts early, before they escalate into more serious disputes and strain community relations,” he said.
On the Seri Kota Public Housing Community Mediation Centre, Aaron said it was JPNIN’s 11th such centre.
Its location was selected based on several factors, including a population of nearly 6,000, available local facilities, community demand and the need to address neighbourhood issues.
He said the centre’s establishment also followed a resolution proposed at the 2024 K2K Initiative Development Strategic Workshop organised by Think City in collaboration with government agencies and stakeholders. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: The abbreviations KPN stand for Kementerian Perpaduan Negara (Ministry of National Unity); JPNIN stands for Jabatan Perpaduan Negara dan Integrasi Nasional (National Unity and Integration Department); BHEUU stands for Bahagian Hal Ehwal Undang-Undang (Legal Affairs Division); and IKLIN stands for Institut Kajian dan Latihan Integrasi Nasional (National Integration Research and Training Institute).

Title: RM5 daily cap proposed as Tawau Hospital parking debate heats up
Article:
TAWAU, Oct 17 — The proposed parking charges at Tawau Hospital should be viewed as a practical solution to persistent parking shortages and security concerns rather than a matter for continued debate.
State Assistant Minister of Health, Women and People’s Wellbeing Datuk Rina Jainal said the provision of paid parking was intended to improve parking management, address concerns over accidents and theft, and enhance security for hospital visitors and staff.
Rina was speaking to reporters after officiating the Tawau Prison Corrective Outreach Programme here on Thursday.
Also present was Tawau Prison director PKK Hasrul Anwar Hasim.
She described the private company’s initiative to develop the hospital’s parking facilities as a step forward, saying the proposal should be assessed based on the needs of the public, patients and hospital staff.
“The initiative can provide facilities for members of the public and visitors from outside the district, while also benefiting hospital staff, following numerous complaints previously received about the shortage of parking spaces,” she said.
The Kukusan assemblywoman said the shortage of parking spaces at Tawau Hospital required practical solutions to ensure greater convenience for visitors and employees.
She urged the public to keep an open mind towards the proposed system, noting that developing and maintaining the parking facilities involved costs and that the land was reportedly owned by an external party rather than the hospital.
Meanwhile, a message circulating online explained that the parking site belonged to Khazanah and had been leased to the Tawau Hospital Staff Association, which pays monthly rental.
According to the message, the proposed paid parking system was intended to help the association cover rental and maintenance costs, including cleaning, with any surplus channelled towards assisting hospital staff and patients.
The proposed parking rates are understood to be RM1 for the first entry for members of the public, followed by RM0.50 for each subsequent hour, capped at RM5 per day. Hospital staff would be charged a monthly rate of RM30. — Daily Express
* Editor’s note: PKK stands for Penolong Komisioner Kanan, the Malay title for Senior Assistant Commissioner, a rank used in the Malaysian Prisons Department.

Title: Driver dies at scene after car crashes into Jalan Hang Tuah monorail pillar in KL
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — A car veered off the road and slammed into a monorail pillar along Jalan Hang Tuah early this morning, killing the 28-year-old driver.
According to Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief Asst Comm Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa, the fatal collision occurred at roughly 3.30am, as reported by
The Star.
The impact trapped the man inside the wrecked vehicle.
Mohd Zamzuri said rescuers managed to extricate him from the vehicle, but he was pronounced dead at the scene due to severe head injuries.
Authorities are currently investigating the circumstances that led to the crash under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, he added.

Title: Border control agency says inter-agency cooperation key to curbing illegal cross-border activities in Kelantan
Article:
PASIR MAS, Oct 17 — Enforcement agencies must strengthen cooperation to ensue more comprehensive border control in Kelantan, especially in curbing cross-border activities through illegal routes.
Rantau Panjang Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) commander Siti Khadijah Hamzah said it oversees five authorised entry points in Kelantan, while other enforcement agencies are responsible for areas that have not been gazetted, in accordance with their respective jurisdictions.
The five entry points are Pengkalan Kubor in Tumpat, Rantau Panjang in Pasir Mas, Bukit Bunga in Tanah Merah, Pelabuhan Tok Bali in Pasir Puteh and Sultan Ismail Petra Airport in Kota Bharu.
“AKPS only has jurisdiction on authorised entry points, while non-gazetted areas fall under the control of other enforcement agencies, including the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), General Operations Force (GOF), Malaysian Army (MAF) and Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency,” she told Bernama at the Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security Complex in Rantau Panjang here recently.
Siti Khadijah said coordination between agencies was crucial to ensuring effective border control, especially in areas with illegal routes.
She said one of the main challenges was the emergence of new routes after existing illegal bases had been shut down, thus the need for continuous monitoring by the relevant agencies.
She added that cross-border activities had also evolved, with movements increasingly shifting to sea routes.
As such, cooperation between land-based and maritime security and enforcement agencies is crucial to curbing cross-border movements through illegal routes and safeguarding the security of Kelantan’s borders. — Bernama

Title: MetMalaysia issues thunderstorm, heavy rain warning for nine states until 3pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm, heavy rain and strong winds warning for nine states until 3pm today.
In a statement, MetMalaysia said the warning covers Bandar Baharu and Kulim in Kedah, the whole of Penang, and several districts in Perak, namely Selama, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Muallim, Kinta, Kampar and Batang Padang.
The same conditions are also expected in Terengganu, covering Kemaman and Dungun, and Pahang, involving Bentong, Jerantut, Kuantan, Maran, Rompin, Pekan, Raub, Cameron Highlands and Lipis.
In Selangor, the affected areas are Hulu Selangor, Gombak and Hulu Langat, while in Negeri Sembilan, they are Seremban and Jelebu. In Johor, the warning covers Pontian, Kota Tinggi, Kulai, Mersing, Segamat and Johor Bahru.
In Sarawak, the affected areas are Betong (Kabong and Saratok), Sibu, Kapit (Song), Sarikei and Mukah. — Bernama

Title: Tired of dodging crow poop, Klang wants to put the birds on the pill
Article:
KLANG, Oct 17 — After shooting nearly 6,000 crows this year, the Klang Royal City Council is weighing a different weapon against the birds of Bandar Bukit Tinggi: contraceptive bird feed.
City councillor Chris Lee, who proposed the trial, said it would move the council away from culling towards a more humane way of controlling the population,
The Star
reported today.
“The oral contraceptive weakens egg yolk membranes to prevent hatching,” he was quoted as saying, adding that the drug is non-lethal.
The idea follows a cull last month in which licensed shooters killed 3,083 crows in a single day in the township and surrounding areas.
Shooting is only a short-term fix, Lee said, because new flocks keep arriving to exploit the same food sources.
Plentiful food and trees to shelter in are the draw, he said, made worse by eateries that dump scraps into drains or fail to dispose of food waste properly.
The township, known for its night stalls and open-air eateries, has seen the crows’ growing numbers raise concern among business owners, shoppers and residents, he said.
Shop owner Ngu Leh Ping, who works at Lorong Batu Nilam 4A, told
The Star
that parked vehicles end up covered in droppings.
Lee said the droppings deface vehicles, shopfronts and outdoor dining furniture, and their acidity speeds up the corrosion of metal fixtures, signage and building facades.
Dried droppings can also harbour fungal spores and bacteria, he said, calling them a potential health risk.
The council will be briefed in a month by the drug’s local distributor in Shah Alam, after discussing the matter with its Health Department’s sub-committee, said its Corporate Communications Department director Norfiza Mahfiz.

Title: DPM Zahid strengthens Malaysia-China ties, advances global TVET cooperation after five-day visit
Article:
TIANJIN, Oct 17 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s five-day working visit to China has strengthened Malaysia-China strategic cooperation in Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), high-tech investment, security and disaster management, thereby opening new opportunities for human capital development and national economic growth.
The October 12-16 visit also saw commitments to expand cooperation in artificial intelligence (AI), semiconductor, electric vehicles (EVs), nuclear technology and digital economy, while also strengthening bilateral ties under the Malaysia-China Comprehensive Strategic Partnership framework.
One of the key focus was the development of the Malaysia-China Institute (MCI) as a strategic platform to strengthen the country’s TVET ecosystem, especially in future industries such as smart manufacturing, robotics, EVs and industrial digitalisation through technology transfer and expertise from strategic partners in China.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister and chairs the National TVET Council, highlighted the importance of the TVET 2.0 approach in closing the gap between educational institutions, industries and the job market, while ensuring that skills training remained relevant with the needs of the rapidly growing high-tech sector.
When delivering the keynote address at the opening of the 2026 World Vocational and Technical Education Development Conference (WVTEDC) in Tianjin yesterday (October 16), he also emphasised the importance of international collaboration in exchanging expertise, developing skills standards and exposure to new technologies to produce a highly skilled workforce.
Malaysia also proposed the establishment of a World TVET Council as a platform to strengthen international cooperation, coordinate the sharing of best practices and drive the development a more integrated global skills ecosystem.
It was proposed that China be made the permanent secretariat or host for the council, thus strengthening the role of Malaysia-China collaboration in advancing the TVET agenda on an international scale.
During the WVTEDC Ministerial Roundtable Meeting, Malaysia also proposed a framework for the mutual recognition of qualifications and cross-border accreditation, while highlighting MCI’s potential in strengthening practical training, technology transfer and trainer development programmes through the Train-the-Trainer approach.
During a bilateral meeting with Chinese Vice-Premier Ding Xuexiang at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on Thursday (October 15), both parties discussed expanding trade, investment and technology cooperation, including the renewal of the Investment Guarantee Agreement (ICA) to strengthen investment protection in strategic and high-impact sectors.
Malaysia also expressed its readiness to act as a bridge between Asean, China and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), including expanding trade and investment cooperation and the use of the Renminbi in related transactions.
In his meeting with Chinese State Councillor and Minister of Public Security Wang Xiaohong in Beijing on Tuesday (October 13), Ahmad Zahid discussed strengthening security cooperation, intelligence sharing and joint operations to combat transnational crime, especially online job scams and cybercrime.
Both parties also focused on finalising the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on security to be signed during Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s visit to Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting (AELM) in November, as well as proposing the resumption of negotiations on an Extradition Treaty and strengthening the implementation of Mutual Legal Assistance (MLA).
Regarding disaster management, Malaysia proposed technical cooperation with China to enhance preparedness for climate change-related risks through the use of satellite monitoring technology, AI and early warning systems, alongside joint training, capacity building, expert exchanges and operational simulations.
The visit also included discussions with China National Nuclear Corporation (CNNC) to explore cooperation in nuclear technology, science and high-tech research and industrial capacity development.
Among the proposals were identifying Malaysian students to pursue studies at suitable higher education institutions in China before undergoing intensive training at CNNC’s training centres and skills institutions, as well as preparing local industries to participate in the nuclear sector’s supply chain.
Overall, Ahmad Zahid’s visit reflected Malaysia’s commitment to strengthening bilateral ties with China through more comprehensive, results-oriented cooperation based on mutual interests, including China’s support for Malaysia’s full participation in Brics.
The two countries also reaffirmed their aspirations to build a High-Level Strategic Malaysia-China Community with a Shared Future for the prosperity of their peoples and regional stability. — Bernama

Title: Suspicious packages at Nilai, Tampin schools: MOE leaves probe to police, says Fadhlina
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 17 — The Education Ministry (MOE) has left the investigation into the discovery of suspicious packages at several schools in Negeri Sembilan yesterday to the police.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the ministry always adopts a vigilant approach towards the discovery of any suspicious items at schools nationwide.
“We urge all principals, headmasters and school personnel to remain vigilant and prepared, especially when it comes to matters involving school safety.
“Once again, we would like to thank the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) for ensuring that all aspects of security are given priority,” she said.
She was speaking to reporters after officiating the ‘Fadhlina Membaca’ Women’s Reading Club with the Education Minister here today.
Yesterday, Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad confirmed that police had received nine reports concerning the discovery of suspicious packages at several schools in Nilai and Tampin.
Alzafny was reported as saying that inspections found all the boxes contained wheat flour and plastic plates. — Bernama

Title: Children must not be stigmatised for life over birth status, says religious affairs minister
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 17 — The public has been reminded not to use a child’s ‘
nasab
’ (birth or lineage) status as a reason to insult, shame or discriminate against them, forcing them to bear a social burden throughout their lives.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said a child should not be blamed for the circumstances of their birth, as Islamic principles clearly state that no individual bears the sins of another.
He said that while legal rulings concerning lineage must be upheld, they should not be used as an excuse to subject children to social judgement.
“Discussions on legal rulings should not be used as a reason to insult, shame or discriminate against a child.
“We need to build a society that can distinguish between evaluating an act and condemning a person for the rest of their life,” he said when delivering his speech at the ‘Seminar Nasab Kebangsaan: Dinamika Cabaran Keluarga Kosmopolitan (SANAD) 2026’, organised by Persatuan Kebajikan Bayt Al-Rahmah, here today.
Zulkifli said society should also be mindful of the language used within families, educational institutions and administrative settings to avoid causing children to bear a prolonged social stigma.
He said the Quranic principle that no individual bears the sins of another should serve as a moral foundation for ensuring that children are not blamed for the circumstances of their birth.
At the same time, Zulkifli said due attention should be given to mothers facing pregnancy or childbirth crises, as they might need assistance in accessing healthcare services, continuing their education and rebuilding their emotional stability.
“They may need support in accessing healthcare services, continuing their education, rebuilding their emotional stability, improving family relationships or planning their future more systematically,” he said.
On the matter of lineage, Zulkifli said it should not be addressed based solely on assumptions, public perceptions or emotions, but required careful examination of the facts, an understanding of syariah principles and consultation with the relevant authorities.
He said the issue also had implications for family matters, inheritance, guardianship, mahram relationships, as well as the naming and registration of births, all of which needed to be examined in accordance with the relevant religious rulings and legal provisions.
He said the management of lineage-related issues should not stop at determining the legal status alone, as attention must also be given to the child’s care, education, protection, well-being and future.
In this regard, he stressed the importance of integrated cooperation among religious institutions, courts, government agencies, welfare organisations, counselling service providers and non-governmental organisations (NGOs) in addressing challenges related to lineage.
“Lineage issues cannot be understood from just one perspective. They require scholarly examination, an understanding of syariah principles, accuracy in legal and administrative matters, as well as concern for the impact on individuals and families,” he said.
Zulkifli said NGOs and shelters also played an important role in identifying gaps in support and unmet needs among mothers and children. — Bernama

Title: Woman sending son to school killed as Hilux hits motorcycle in Kota Marudu; teen dies in separate Tawau collision
Article:
KOTA MARUDU, Oct 17 — A woman on her way to send her son to school was killed when the motorcycle she was riding was involved in an accident at the Kampung Marak Parak junction, here, early yesterday.
Liza Jius, 34, died at the scene from severe head injuries, while her seven-year-old son, who was riding pillion and attends Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Marak Parak, sustained minor injuries.
District Police Chief Supt Simiun Lomudin said the accident occurred at about 6.19am and involved the Modenas Kriss and a Toyota Hilux driven by a 40-year-old man.
“The Hilux driver was believed to have been overtaking the motorcycle in front of him when it turned right to enter the school junction, resulting in a collision,” he said.
Investigations were ongoing under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
In TAWAU, a 19-year-old motorcyclist was killed in a collision involving a Perodua Axia at Batu 3, Jalan Apas, at about 12.30pm yesterday.
District Fire and Rescue Station Chief Deputy Superintendent of Fire and Rescue II Jemishin Ujin said Mohd Adrian was pronounced dead at the scene.
“The car’s 31-year-old female driver and 40-year-old female front passenger sustained minor injuries in the accident,” he told
Daily Express
.
Jemishin said the front passenger was trapped in the vehicle before firefighters rescued her using hydraulic cutting equipment and handed her over to Health Ministry personnel for further treatment. — Daily Express

Title: Immigration detains 190 foreigners, two locals in Pudu entertainment centre crackdown
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — The Immigration Department detained 190 foreigners and two local men during a raid on an entertainment centre in Pudu here early today following public complaints about disturbances.
Its Enforcement Division director, Datuk Basri Othman, said those detained comprised 99 men and 91 women, aged between 20 and 41.
Of the foreigners, 188 were Indonesians, while the other two were from Bangladesh and India.
The two local men are believed to be the employer and caretaker of the entertainment centre, which is located about 10 metres from a mosque.
“Several rooms in the premises were used for entertainment, with between 50 and 60 people in each room at the time of the raid. Immigration offences detected included overstaying and not possessing valid travel documents,” he told reporters after the operation.
All those detained were taken to an immigration depot for investigation under Sections 6(1)(c) and 15(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63.
During the raid, Bernama observed white powder suspected to be drugs on several plates, as well as condoms in the rooms.
Basri said further investigations would be conducted into the possibility of immoral activities at the premises. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia Airlines to resume Jeddah, Madinah services tomorrow after safety review
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 17 — Malaysia Airlines will resume scheduled flight operations to and from Jeddah and Madinah, Saudi Arabia, effective tomorrow (October 18) following a comprehensive safety review and operational risk assessment.
The national carrier advised passengers travelling to or from the two destinations to check their flight schedules and ensure their contact details are updated via the “My Booking” feature on its website or mobile application.
“Passengers who made their bookings through third-party platforms or travel agents are advised to contact their respective booking providers directly regarding their travel arrangements,” it said in a statement today.
Malaysia Airlines said customers requiring assistance could use the Live Chat feature on its website or contact its Global Contact Centre at 1 300 88 3000 (within Malaysia) or +603 7843 3000 (international).
The airline also thanked passengers for their patience and understanding during the temporary suspension of flights to the two destinations.
It said it would continue to closely monitor developments in the region, with the safety and security of passengers and crew remaining its highest priority. — Bernama

Title: Motorist escapes injury after tree branch falls on car in Ipoh
Article:
IPOH, Oct 17 — A 31-year-old motorist escaped unhurt after a tree branch fell onto his Perodua Myvi in front of the Kuala Kangsar Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) office this morning.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department assistant director (Operations) Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the department received an emergency call at 8.57am, prompting seven personnel from the Kuala Kangsar Fire and Rescue Station to rush to the scene.
The driver had managed to get out of the vehicle before the firemen arrived.
Preliminary investigations found that a branch from a tree believed to be more than 50 years old had become brittle and fallen onto the car. No heavy rain or storm was reported at the time of the incident.
Sabarodzi said firefighters used a chainsaw to remove the fallen branch, and the operation ended at 9.20am. — Bernama

Title: Loke: We cannot stop foreigners from using public buses, but all passengers must comply with rules
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 17 — The government cannot stop foreigners from using public buses, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said today when asked about complaints of unruly behaviour by foreigners on buses.
“We cannot stop foreigners from taking public buses,” he said.
“Public buses are public transport and everyone has the right to use them,” Loke said at a press conference after launching Rapid Penang’s electric buses at the depot in Weld Quay here.
However, Loke said all passengers, regardless of nationality, must comply with the rules and behave appropriately.
He said complaints about unruly behaviour should be reported to the bus operator or the relevant authorities, which could then take action based on the circumstances.
Complaints about foreigners behaving disruptively on public buses have previously surfaced on social media and in local news reports, including allegations of loud conversations, blocking aisles, failing to queue and refusing to follow instructions from bus staff.
Such complaints have also prompted calls for passengers to respect other commuters, keep noise levels down, avoid obstructing entrances and exits, and comply with safety instructions.
Meanwhile, Loke cautioned that the introduction of quieter electric buses must be accompanied by greater public awareness to protect pedestrians.
“We will see newer buses that are more environmentally friendly and quieter. But there is also a risk, because when they pass, many people do not realise a bus is passing,” he said.
He called on the authorities to account for the change as the state gradually renews its bus fleet.
“I hope the state government, the city council and others will take this into account in traffic planning and pedestrian routes, particularly at pedestrian crossings,” he said.
Rapid Penang began operating 15 electric buses today, comprising 14 measuring 8.25 metres and one measuring 12 metres.
The electric buses are equipped with an Acoustic Vehicle Alerting System that produces external warning sounds to help pedestrians and other road users detect their presence, particularly at low speeds.
The buses also have an Advanced Driver Assistance System that provides driving assistance and warnings to bus captains.
Loke said the transition involved more than introducing vehicles with new technology.
“Operational readiness, charging facilities, maintenance and workforce capabilities must be strengthened alongside implementation,” he said.
Rapid Penang is scheduled to receive a total of 75 electric buses by March 2027 under the first procurement phase, which also includes 175 buses for Rapid KL.

Title: Exercise freedom on social media with respect, courtesy, says King
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 17 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, has reminded the public that freedom comes with responsibility and called for social media users to engage with respect and courtesy.
Sultan Ibrahim, who is also Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Chancellor, said this in response to the misuse of social media by certain quarters to incite others, spread hatred and sow division in society.
“Do not turn social media into a platform to insult, swear at, vilify or humiliate others. Differences of opinion are no reason for hostility. We may disagree, but we must express our views in respectful and courteous language.
“If you wish to criticise, do so constructively. If you wish to correct someone, do so with tact and consideration,” His Majesty said.
Sultan Ibrahim was speaking at the 105th UiTM Convocation Ceremony at the Tuanku Canselor Grand Hall, UiTM Shah Alam, here today.
Also present was Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor, Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin, who is also UiTM Pro-Chancellor.
Sultan Ibrahim also called on the public not to misuse artificial intelligence (AI) technology to create fake images and videos with the intention of insulting or embarrassing others.
His Majesty said that behind every name and face subjected to hatred and insults was a person with a family, dignity and feelings.
“From a young age, we are taught to respect our elders, speak with decorum, and not look down on others on the basis of religion or race, because good manners are not merely about politeness, but are the lifeblood of the nation’s dignity.
“However, amid today’s advances in digital technology and social media, some have forgotten their manners and feel free to insult, abuse, verbally attack and humiliate others,” His Majesty said.
In this regard, Sultan Ibrahim urged the public not to readily believe or share any news without first verifying its authenticity.
“Do not let our haste to be the first to share unverified information turn us into people who spread slander and hatred.
“I want to see us become a mature society in our communication, free to express ourselves with courtesy, bold enough to share our views without insulting others, and firm in defending our convictions without sowing hatred,” His Majesty said.
At the ceremony, Sultan Ibrahim also consented to the UiTM campus in Jalan Othman, Petaling Jaya, being renamed the Tun Arshad Ayub Campus in recognition of his services and contributions to spearheading the establishment and development of UiTM since 1965.
The late Arshad, who died in 2022, was the first director of the MARA Institute of Technology (ITM) from 1967 to 1975. The institution, now known as UiTM, regarded him as a pioneer who laid the groundwork for its educational development.
His Majesty also congratulated all graduates, parents and the university community on their achievements, expressing hope that UiTM would continue to progress in producing successful graduates for the nation’s progress.
The convocation ceremony, which was also attended by Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abdul Kadir and UiTM vice-chancellor Professor Datuk Shahrin Sahib @ Sahibuddin, will see a total of 32,630 graduates receive diplomas and degrees in various fields from today until December 16.
UiTM also conferred the title of Professor Emeritus on Datuk Dr Roziah Mohd Janor, its first female former vice-chancellor. — Bernama

Title: Ranau and Kundasang roads buried in mud after heavy rain, authorities warn of more landslides
Article:
RANAU, Oct 17 — Heavy rain on Thursday triggered mudflows and landslides at several locations around Ranau and Kundasang, leaving roads covered in mud, rocks and debris and prompting authorities to step up safety monitoring.
The affected areas include Jalan Kundasang-Mohimboyon, Kampung Lipantai, Kibbas-Tambiau and the Mohimboyon-Kundasang Lama route, according to the Karanaan Community Development Leader’s Unit (UPPM).
The muddy conditions posed hazards to motorists and motorcyclists, particularly along roads where mud and rocks had spilled onto the surface.
Ranau District Police Chief Supt Mursalin Mahmud urged residents and road users to remain vigilant, warning that continued rainfall could trigger flash floods and further landslides.
Police received a report of a mudflow along Jalan Kundasang-Mohimboyon and deployed personnel to the location at 6.15pm.
Upon arrival, officers found that clean-up work was already underway using two machines and eight workers.
The affected section, estimated at about 20ft by 40ft, was subsequently cleared, and the road was reported passable in both directions.
No casualties were reported.
Mursalin urged residents to report incidents promptly so authorities could assess the situation and provide assistance where necessary, adding that Ranau police remained on standby to safeguard public safety.
Meanwhile, four personnel from the Ranau Civil Defence Force monitored flood-prone locations, including Sungai Mansahaban and Sungai Liwagu, as well as a blocked drain at the Takurik junction along Jalan Sinarut Baru.
The inspection found that branches had obstructed the drain, and personnel removed them to restore water flow.
Water levels at Sungai Mansahaban and Sungai Liwagu remained under control during the monitoring exercise and had not affected nearby homes.
Light rain was reported at the time, with no emergency incidents recorded.
Civil Defence personnel advised residents to remain alert and move to safer locations if water levels rose, while contacting emergency services if assistance was needed.
Separately, the Civil Defence Force’s Kundasang unit monitored a landslide at Kampung Himbaan reported at 4pm.
Three personnel inspected the area and identified four landslide locations along the route, as well as water flowing across the road surface.
The affected slope was estimated to be about 20ft high and five metres wide.
Initial checks were conducted to assess road conditions and protect road users.
No casualties were reported during the inspection, and monitoring was to continue as rainfall persisted.
Residents and motorists were advised to avoid hazardous areas and remain alert to possible further slope failures.
Authorities said monitoring operations had not identified any affected villages, schools, buildings, healthcare facilities or roads requiring evacuation.
No temporary relief centres had been opened at the time of the Civil Defence assessment.
The authorities urged the public to take extra precautions during prolonged wet weather, avoid driving through dangerous sections and report any sudden rise in water levels, mudflows or fresh ground movement.
For emergencies in the Kundasang area, the public can contact the NG999 emergency line or the Kundasang Operations Control Centre at 088-888991. — Daily Express
* Editor’s note: The initials UPPM in Malay stands for Unit Pemimpin Pembangunan Masyarakat, or Community Development Leader’s Unit in English.

Title: Putrajaya mulls longer jail terms, higher fines for rail cable theft to protect public safety, says Loke
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 17 — The Transport Ministry is working with the Home Ministry on legal amendments to impose heavier penalties for cable theft affecting the country’s rail networks, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said today.
“The details have not been finalised,” Loke said.
“We are still at the policy discussion stage on increasing prison sentences and fines,” he told a press conference after launching Rapid Penang’s electric buses at the depot in Weld Quay here.
He was responding to a question about a reported cable theft on the MRT Kajang Line and whether the government would strengthen penalties against offenders.
Loke said the problem extended beyond the MRT network, with other rail operators, including Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad, also affected.
“Even the ECRL, which has yet to begin operations, has had cables stolen,” he said.
He said tougher punishment was needed to send a clear message to offenders.
“This is not ordinary theft. Cable theft involves the safety of the public,” he said.
Loke also stressed that operators must take preventive action while the government worked on the proposed amendments.
“This includes installing CCTV cameras at strategic locations and deploying more auxiliary police officers to ensure our restricted areas are not intruded upon by cable thieves,” he said.

Title: Loke: Rapid Penang starts electric bus services with 15 vehicles, targets 75 by March 2027
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 17 — Rapid Penang began operating its first 15 electric buses today, marking the start of its transition towards an electric bus fleet, said Transport Minister Anthony Loke today.
“There will be new buses arriving every month to complete Rapid Penang’s fleet of 75 buses by March next year,” he told a press conference after launching the service at the Rapid Penang Depot in Weld Quay here.
He said the initial fleet comprises 14 buses measuring 8.25 metres and one measuring 12 metres.
“The shorter buses make it easier to travel, particularly on the island, where they can enter narrower roads and more densely populated areas,” he said.
Loke linked the rollout to Penang’s efforts to reduce carbon emissions.
“This is part of the public transport sector’s contribution towards a more environmentally friendly state,” he said.
According to a statement issued by Rapid Bus, the first procurement phase involved 250 electric buses across Rapid Penang and Rapid KL, with 175 allocated to the latter.
At the press conference, Loke clarified that the estimated RM200 million investment covered all 250 buses under this phase.
The procurement is divided into two delivery stages to coordinate the arrival of buses with charging infrastructure readiness and depot requirements.
Under the first stage, Loke said Rapid Penang would receive 40 buses and Rapid KL 110.
Deliveries began in June and are scheduled to be completed by December 31.
He said the second stage involved another 35 buses for Penang and 65 for Rapid KL, with deliveries expected to begin in January and finish by March 2027.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke inspects charging station for the new EV buses at the Rapid Penang Depot October 17, 2026. — Picture by Opalyn Mok
Loke said 150 charging units had been installed at nine depots, including three in Penang, to support the first delivery stage.
Another 100 charging units are planned at six depots, including two in Penang, for the second stage, he added.
He said they have received 52 electric buses for both Rapid KL and Rapid Penang as of October 13.
He explained that the phased introduction would allow it to monitor performance, reliability and maintenance requirements to ensure service continuity.
The buses are equipped with an Advanced Driver Assistance System, which provides driving assistance and alerts to bus captains.
The buses are also equipped with an Acoustic Vehicle Alerting System, which produces external warning sounds to alert pedestrians and other road users, particularly at low speeds.
Loke said the rollout forms part of Prasarana Malaysia Berhad’s plan to acquire 1,600 electric buses between 2026 and 2031 to replace part of the existing diesel fleet across Rapid Penang and Rapid KL.
In his speech, Loke also outlined the bus operator’s future role alongside the Mutiara Line LRT.
“Rapid Penang, as the stage bus operator in Penang, must play a supporting role to ensure first- and last-mile connections are improved and complement this transport system,” he said.

Title: Nik Nazmi confirms he was one of two caught in Petaling Jaya Jais raid, apologises to wife and family
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — Bersama leader Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad has confirmed that he is one of the two individuals involved in an incident with the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais) in Petaling Jaya on Thursday.
In a statement addressing the incident, Nik Nazmi admitted his fault and confirmed that he was the man caught with a woman, who is not his
muhrim
(a legally permissible close relative), in an enclosed space.
The statement was issued publicly by Nik Nazmi in response to reports regarding the Jais operation.
“I admit that it is a mistake,” he said.
Nik Nazmi explained that he and his colleagues began a discussion at their studio in Brickfields, Kuala Lumpur, and later decided to continue the meeting in Petaling Jaya to review materials related to a project.
He stated that when the Jais officers arrived, only he and the woman were present.
However, he stressed that they did not commit any indecent acts that would arouse suspicion, noting that he had also informed the Jais officer of this at the time.
Nik Nazmi publicly apologised to his wife, family, and all those affected by his lapse in judgment during the incident.
He also apologised to Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) for disappointing its members and supporters, acknowledging that the issue has damaged the party.
“I will give my cooperation to any legal process,” he said.
Nik Nazmi added that he would accept any decision made by the party and urged all parties to respect the legal process and refrain from prolonging discussions through the media.
